subject: chemistry-1
question: Ammonium sulfate, (NH4)2SO4, contains 15 atoms per formula unit and dissolves in water to give NH4+ and SO4 2- ions. Which statement best explains the bonding present in this compound?

options.text: Every bond in the compound is ionic, because the substance is a salt that separates into ions in water.
Every bond in the compound is covalent, because the formula contains only nonmetal atoms.
The N-H and S-O bonds are ionic, while the attraction between the two polyatomic ions is covalent.
Covalent bonds hold the atoms together within each polyatomic ion, while ionic attractions hold NH4+ and SO4 2- to one another.

explanation:
Compounds built from polyatomic ions display both bonding types at once: shared electron pairs bind N to H and S to O inside each ion, while electrostatic attraction between the resulting NH4+ and SO4 2- units builds the lattice. That is precisely why dissolution releases intact polyatomic ions instead of free N, H, S, and O atoms, ruling out option A. Option B ignores that a cation and an anion are present despite the all-nonmetal composition, and option C reverses the two bond types. Counting confirms the composition: 2 x (1 + 4) + 1 + 4 = 15 atoms per formula unit.

ELI-10: Polyatomic ions force you to look at two levels at once. Inside NH4+, nitrogen and hydrogen share electron pairs, and inside SO4 2-, sulfur and oxygen do the same, so those internal links are covalent and survive dissolving. Between the two clusters there is nothing shared at all, only a positive group attracted to a negative group, which is ionic. The all-nonmetal formula fools people into calling it purely covalent, but the ions in solution prove otherwise. Atom count: two NH4 groups give 2 x 5 = 10, plus one S and four O, for 15.
